title: Two people's appointments in very similar words
description: Dad and Mum each have a dentist appointment at the same practice, written in almost the same words. Neither changes. A brain that treats the second note as an update to the first loses Dad's appointment.

notes.text: Dad's dentist appointment is Tuesday 10 March at 10:00 at Park Dental.
Bought bread and milk on the way home.
Mum's dentist appointment is Thursday 12 March at 14:00 at Park Dental.
Joan next door will water the plants while we are away.
Dad's hearing test is Friday 20 March at 11:30 at the clinic.
Took Mum to the garden centre. She chose two pots of lavender.
Boiler service done. The engineer says it is fine for another year.
Mum's friend Rita rang. They are going for lunch on Sunday.
The car is booked in for its MOT on 25 March.
Parking at Park Dental is free for an hour.

questions.why: They are two people's separate appointments. Replacing the first with the second would lose Dad's.
Mum's similar note must not have deleted it.
The later note must itself be found.
A third note about Dad shares his name and words but is a different appointment.
